import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_2.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df_movies = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_33_0: ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
df_users = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)   # Source3_33_1: ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']
df_ratings = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0) # Source3_33_2: ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']

# Step 1: Join ratings with movies on 'movie_id' to get 'title'
df_ratings_movies = pd.merge(df_ratings, df_movies[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='left')

# Step 2: Join the above result with users on 'user_id' to get 'age' and 'occupation'
df_full = pd.merge(df_ratings_movies, df_users[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='left')

# Step 3: According to target schema:
# ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]

# Convert data types accordingly:
# - title: string (already string)
# - user_id: float (source is int, convert to float)
# - movie_id: integer (should be int)
# - rating: float (already float or int, convert to float)
# - timestamp: float (int timestamp, convert to float)
# - age: float (int in source, convert to float)
# - occupation: float (int in source, convert to float)

df_full['title'] = df_full['title'].astype(str)
df_full['user_id'] = df_full['user_id'].astype(float)
df_full['movie_id'] = df_full['movie_id'].astype(int)
df_full['rating'] = df_full['rating'].astype(float)
df_full['timestamp'] = df_full['timestamp'].astype(float)
df_full['age'] = df_full['age'].astype(float)
df_full['occupation'] = df_full['occupation'].astype(float)

# Step 4: Select and reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df_target = df_full[['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']]

# Step 5: Save the transformed dataframe to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_33_2 with Source3_33_1 on user_id
join_1 = pd.merge(source2, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_33_0 on movie_id
join_2 = pd.merge(join_1, source0, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns in target schema: title (string), user_id (float but used as group key), movie_id (int)
# Aggregations on rating, timestamp, age, occupation by mean
grouped = join_2.groupby(["title", "user_id", "movie_id"], as_index=False).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean",
    "age": "mean",
    "occupation": "mean"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
result = grouped[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

# Write to target CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_33/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
